```{=typst}
#set par(justify: false)

#show raw: set text(font: "Fira Code")
// software names: monospace + deep blue, except inside code chunks
// (sized by the inline raw rule below)
#let in-code = state("in-code", false)
#show regex("\\b(txomics/tapir|tximeta|plyxp|splicelogic|tapir|TAPIR|plyranges|tidyomics|oarfish|bambu|DESeq2|satuRn|TreeTerminus|terminus|treeclimbR|stageR|tidySummarizedExperiment|dplyr|Biostrings|DRIMSeq|edgeR|Biosurfer|rlang|salmon|Snakemake)\\b"): it => context {
  if in-code.get() { it } else { text(fill: rgb("#2B6CA3"), raw(it.text)) }
}
// inline code in slide text: scale up from raw's 0.8em (not inside chunks)
#show raw.where(block: false): it => context {
  if in-code.get() { it } else { text(size: 1.15em, it) }
}

  in-code.update(true)
  set text(size: 24pt)
  set par(leading: 0.5em)
  let blocks = []
  for ln in sourcelines { blocks = blocks + ln + EndLine() }

  in-code.update(false)
}
```

# Why new syntax (for humans or LLMs)?

```{=typst}
#let detail(body) = text(size: 16pt, fill: luma(110), body)
#{
  set list(spacing: 1em)
  set par(leading: 0.5em)
  [
    - Humans read and review code (for now) \
      #detail[Concise and easy to comprehend]
    - Grammar enables precision while maintaining readability, e.g. \
      #detail[“find peaks near DE genes” vs. \
      \
      `genes |> filter(de) |> promoters(...) |> join_overlap_inner(peaks, ...)`] \
    - Composable verbs map meaningfully to many analyses \
      #detail[With standard data classes, this catches silent bookkeeping & genomics errors]
    - Tested, maintained verbs safer than freshly generated code \
      #detail[And the same verbs work consistently across backends]
  ]
}
```

# Multi-sample long-read RNA-seq workflow

```{=typst}
#notes[Long reads capture near-complete transcripts, but short-read
  multi-sample methods don't transfer directly. Gaps: provenance of novel
  transcripts, event detection from whole transcripts, isoform-level
  inference. Our tools in blue: tximeta, plyxp, splicelogic.]
#let unc = rgb("#4B9CD3")
#let stage(title, tools, desc, ours: false) = block(
  width: 100%, height: 100%, inset: (x: 5pt, y: 4pt), radius: 4pt,
  fill: if ours { unc.lighten(80%) } else { luma(240) },
  stroke: if ours { 1.5pt + unc } else { 0.5pt + luma(180) },
  align(center + horizon, {
    set par(leading: 0.35em)
    stack(
      text(size: 14pt, weight: "bold", fill: rgb("#13294B"), title),
      ..if tools != none { (v(0.3em), text(size: 13pt, tools)) },
      v(0.5em),
      text(size: 11pt, fill: luma(80), desc))
  }))
#let arrow-glyph = text(size: 20pt, fill: luma(120), sym.arrow.r)
#let arrow = align(center + horizon, arrow-glyph)
#let gap = 0.5cm
#v(0.6em)
#grid(
  columns: (1.15fr, 1cm, 1fr, auto, 1fr, auto, 1fr, auto, 1fr, auto, 1fr),
  rows: 4.6cm,
  column-gutter: 4pt,
  block(height: 100%, grid(rows: (1fr, 1fr), row-gutter: gap,
    stage("Annotate", none)[reference + filtering],
    stage("Detect", none)[novel transcripts])),
  block(height: 100%, grid(rows: (1fr, 1fr), row-gutter: gap,
    align(center + horizon, rotate(30deg, arrow-glyph)),
    align(center + horizon, rotate(-30deg, arrow-glyph)))),
  stage("Quantify")[oarfish bambu][on cluster or cloud (AnVIL)],
  arrow,
  stage("Import", ours: true)[tximeta][automatic provenance of annotated + novel],
  arrow,
  stage("Manipulate", ours: true)[plyxp][tidy verbs applied to standard data objects],
  arrow,
  stage("Test")[DESeq2 satuRn][assessing differences across samples],
  arrow,
  stage("Interpret", ours: true)[splicelogic plyranges][deducing causes and consequences],
)
#v(0.8em)
#align(center, text(size: 13pt, fill: luma(80))[
  #box(width: 0.9em, height: 0.9em, radius: 2pt, baseline: 0.1em,
    fill: unc.lighten(80%), stroke: 1.5pt + unc)
  #h(0.2em) recent work from the lab])
```

# Provenance: tximeta for reference + novel

```{=typst}
#sticker("tximeta")
```

- Quantifiers record a digest of the reference transcripts
- tximeta matches digests at import, attaches transcript metadata
- No manual tracking of annotation sources or releases
- Long-read indices mix annotated and novel transcripts
- tximeta now checks each digest separately

# tximeta: mixed reference workflow

```{=typst}
#sticker("tximeta")
#align(center, image("images/mixed-ref-diagram.png", height: 10.5cm))
#notes[oarfish records a digest per sub-index: annotated (e.g. GENCODE) and
  novel (e.g. bambu, de novo, spike-ins, fusions); salmon via a Snakemake rule
  writing `mixed_ref_digests.json`. `importData()` reads counts + digests;
  `inspectDigests()` checks each against the digest table and
  linkedTxome / linkedTxpData; `updateMetadata()` attaches what matches.]
```

# tximeta: import, inspect, link, update

```{=typst}
#sticker("tximeta")
#notes[`importData()`: counts + per-sub-index digests (salmon: add
  `mixedDigest = "mixed_ref_digests.json"`). `inspectDigests()`: annotated
  matches GENCODE v48, novel has no match. `makeLinkedTxpData()`: register
  novel transcripts once in the file cache. `updateMetadata(ranges = TRUE)`:
  metadata + ranges for both sets. Still open: subsets of the annotation.]
```

```{r}
se <- importData(coldata, type = "oarfish")
inspectDigests(se)
#> index     source  organism release genome ...
#> annotated GENCODE Homo sa… 48      GRCh38 ...
#> novel     <NA>    <NA>     <NA>    <NA>   ...

# <add or link metadata in local cache>
se <- updateMetadata(se, ranges = TRUE)
```

# plyxp: a grammar for annotated matrices

```{=typst}
#sticker("plyxp")
#student("justinlandis", "Justin Landis")
```

- SummarizedExperiment links counts to transcript and sample data
- plyxp brings dplyr verbs to SummarizedExperiment objects
- Each expression is scoped: assays, `rows()`, or `cols()`
- Pronouns like `.rows` and `.cols` reach across contexts
- Explicit and efficient; now inside tidySummarizedExperiment

# plyxp: mutate, filter, aggregate

```{=typst}
#sticker("plyxp")
#notes[`mutate()` in the assays context: scale counts by row data
  (`.rows$tx_length`) and column data (`.cols$size_factor`). `rows()` /
  `cols()` write to rowData / colData; `.assays_asis` gives the native matrix
  for `rowMeans()`. `filter()` subsets by metadata. `group_by(rows(gene_id))` +
  `summarize()` aggregates isoforms to genes. Timing: 4.7 ms native, 19 ms
  plyxp, 372 ms unwound to a long table.]
```

```{r}
xp <- new_plyxp(se) |>
  mutate(
    cts_bp = counts / .rows$tx_length,
    norm = counts / .cols$size_factor,
    rows(ave = rowMeans(.assays_asis$counts)),
    cols(trt = condition == "trt")) |>
  filter(rows(ave > 10), cols(batch != "b3"))

genes <- xp |>
  group_by(rows(gene_id)) |>
  summarize(counts = colSums(counts))
```

# splicelogic: from transcripts to events

```{=typst}
#sticker("splicelogic")
#student("beatrizcampillo", "Beatriz Campillo")
```

- Splicing changes rarely come one event at a time
- Short-read methods lack full-transcript context for events
- splicelogic turns any two transcript sets into events
- Works with any DTU method, or novel vs. annotated
- Events are genomic ranges, ready for plyranges and Biostrings

# splicelogic: events as composable ranges

```{=typst}
#sticker("splicelogic")
#notes[`prepare_exons()` from DTU results of any method (satuRn, DRIMSeq,
  edgeR), or `prepare_exons_by_partition()` for two transcript sets, e.g.
  novel vs. annotated. `find_all_events()`: nine event types (SE, IE, MXE, RI,
  SI, A5SS, A3SS, ATSS, ATES). Skipped exons, then 100 bp upstream intron, then
  sequence: in GTEx PTBP1 knockdown these recover PTBP1's binding preference.
  `%>%` needed for the `.` placeholder.]
```

```{r}
# <ranges> to <ranges>: "endomorphic"
events <- exons |> find_all_events()

skipped <- exons |>
  find_skipped_exons() |>
  flank_upstream(100) %>%
  mutate(intron_seq = get_seq(., "hg38"))

# metadata attached to ranges as columns
skipped$intron_seq
```

```{=typst}
#student("rachelsharp", "Rachel Sharp")
```

- A collaboration with Stephanie Hicks's lab at JHU
- Sowmya Parthiban (Hicks lab) and the Love lab
- Chapters are being re-organized by Dr. Rachel Sharp
- Code and docs: [txomics/tapir](https://txomics.github.io/tapir/)

# Back to the question: why new syntax?

```{=typst}
#align(center, image("images/finally.png", height: 6cm))
```

- tximeta: provenance travels with the data, no silent mismatches
- plyxp: scoped verbs on standard objects, short and reviewable
- splicelogic: ranges in, ranges out --- composes with plyranges
- Write the intent; tested verbs handle the bookkeeping
